about: The scripted AI lesson for g5-nigeria (2026-11-19, Phase B, brief docs/briefs/2026-11-15-script-four-topics.md): every word she sees is written here once and checked (tools/check-script.js, tools/review-lesson.js --script). The AI only marks her typed answers (choosing a branch written here), answers her own questions, and sorts her messages. It opens with two recall questions from g5-development.

steps.text: Welcome! This lesson is a case study of one country, Nigeria: where it is, why it matters, how its economy is changing, and what that means for its people and its environment.

steps.question: First, two quick questions from the last lesson. A country whose economy has started to grow fast as it builds up industry is called…?
steps.right: Yes: an NEE, a newly emerging economy.

wrong.other: Not quite: an NEE, a newly emerging economy.
wrong.lic: Not quite: an LIC is one of the poorest countries. Fast growth through industry makes an NEE.
wrong.hic: Not quite: an HIC is already rich. Fast growth through industry makes an NEE.

idk.hint: The E stands for "economy" and the N for "newly". Which button is it?

steps.answerWhy: A country growing fast as it builds up industry is an NEE, a newly emerging economy.

steps.question: Second: which measure is an average income for each person in a country?

wrong.life: Not quite: life expectancy is how long people live. GNI per head is the average income.
wrong.imr: Not quite: that counts babies dying. GNI per head is the average income.

steps.answerWhy: GNI per head is the country's income shared out equally between its people.

steps.text: Now this lesson. Nigeria is in West Africa, on the coast of the Gulf of Guinea. With about 238 million people, it has more people than any other African country.
Nigeria is an NEE. Its economy is worth about $291 billion a year, but its GNI per head is only $1,360, so many Nigerians are still poor.
Within West Africa, Nigeria has the biggest economy. That is its regional importance: how much it matters within its own part of the world.
Nigeria is the biggest member of ECOWAS, a group of West African countries working to make trade between them easier.
Globally, across the whole world, Nigeria matters as a big oil exporter, and its films and music are watched and heard far beyond Africa.

steps.question: An exam asks: "Outline one way in which Nigeria is regionally important." Which answer fits?

options.text: It has the biggest economy in West Africa
It sells oil all around the world

steps.right: Yes: regional means within its part of the world, West Africa.

wrong.other: Not quite: it has the biggest economy in West Africa.
wrong.global: Selling oil worldwide is global importance. Regional means within West Africa: it has the biggest economy there.
wrong.city: True, but that is about inside Nigeria. Regional means within West Africa: it has the biggest economy there.

idk.hint: Regional means within its world region. Which option mentions West Africa?

steps.answerWhy: Regionally, within West Africa, Nigeria has the biggest economy.

steps.text: The wider context of the country matters too. Britain ruled Nigeria until independence; since then there have been military governments as well as elected ones.
Socially and culturally, Nigeria has hundreds of ethnic groups: the Hausa-Fulani in the mostly Muslim north, the Yoruba and Igbo in the mostly Christian south.
Environmentally, the north is dry grassland. The south has rainforest and the Niger Delta: the large wetland where the River Niger reaches the sea, and where most of Nigeria's oil comes from.

steps.prompt: In one line: give one reason Nigeria is important regionally and one reason it is important globally.
points: regionally: the biggest economy in West Africa (or biggest member of ECOWAS)
globally: a big oil exporter (or films and music known worldwide)
steps.idk: No problem. A good line would be: regionally it has West Africa's biggest economy; globally it is a big oil exporter.

steps.text: An economy has sectors. The primary sector takes raw materials from the land or sea: farming, fishing and oil.
The secondary sector makes things in factories: manufacturing.
The tertiary sector provides services, such as shops, banks, health care and films.

steps.question: Which sector is a bank in Lagos part of?
steps.right: Yes: a bank provides a service, so it is tertiary.

wrong.other: Not quite: tertiary, because a bank provides a service.
wrong.primary: Not quite: primary takes raw materials from the land or sea. A bank provides a service: tertiary.
wrong.secondary: Not quite: secondary makes things in factories. A bank provides a service: tertiary.

idk.hint: Does a bank take raw materials, make things, or provide a service?

steps.answerWhy: A bank provides a service, so it is in the tertiary sector.

steps.text: Oil, from the Niger Delta, is the big earner. In 2025 fuel made up about 86% of the goods Nigeria sold abroad. But oil gives few jobs, because machines do most of the work.
When the world oil price falls, Nigeria's income falls with it, so depending on oil is risky.
The balance between sectors is shifting. In 2025 services were about 58% of the economy, industry about 16% and farming about 23%, though farming still gave about a third of all jobs.
Factories in and around Lagos, Nigeria's biggest city, make food, drinks, cement and soap. Nollywood, Nigeria's film industry, is a growing service.
Manufacturing can stimulate development. A new factory pays regular wages; workers spend them in local shops, which then need more staff; the government collects more tax for schools and roads.
One new business leading to many more jobs and more tax in this way is called the multiplier effect.

steps.question: A new cement factory opens near Lagos. Which shows the multiplier effect?

options.text: Its workers spend wages in local shops, which take on more staff

steps.right: Yes: one factory's wages create more jobs in other businesses.

wrong.other: Not quite: workers spend wages in local shops, which take on more staff.
wrong.cement: Not quite: making cement is just its product. The multiplier is the chain: wages are spent in shops, which take on more staff.
wrong.export: Not quite: selling abroad is trade. The multiplier is the chain: wages are spent locally, so shops take on more staff.

idk.hint: The multiplier is about one job leading to others. Which option has a chain?

steps.answerWhy: Wages spent in local shops create more jobs there: the multiplier effect.

steps.prompt: In one line: how can a new factory help a country develop?
points: wages are spent locally, creating more jobs (the multiplier effect)
the government collects more tax for services
steps.idk: No problem. A good line would be: a factory gives jobs, the wages are spent locally to create more jobs, and taxes pay for schools and roads.

keyPoints.heading: TNCs in Nigeria: Shell and Unilever

steps.text: A TNC, or transnational corporation, is a company that works in many countries. Its headquarters are usually in a rich country.

Shell, an oil company based in the UK, took oil from the Niger Delta on land for decades. In 2025 it sold that business to a Nigerian-owned company, but it still produces oil from deep water off the coast.
Unilever makes soap, food and drinks in factories in Nigeria, and buys from Nigerian suppliers.
Advantages: TNCs give jobs and train workers in new skills; they pay taxes that fund schools and clinics; they build roads and bring new technology.
When a foreign company sends its profits back to its home country instead of spending them where they were earned, that is profit repatriation. Less of the money then helps Nigerians.
Oil spills from pipelines, some from leaks and some from theft, have polluted creeks, farmland and fishing grounds in the Niger Delta.
Burning off the spare gas that comes up with oil, instead of using it, is called gas flaring. It wastes fuel and pollutes the air.
The picture weighs up what oil brings Nigeria and what it costs.

steps.question: Which is a disadvantage of TNCs such as Shell for Nigeria?

options.text: Much of the profit goes back to the company's home country
They pay taxes to the Nigerian government

steps.right: Yes: profit repatriation means less money stays in Nigeria.

wrong.other: Not quite: much of the profit goes back to the home country.
wrong.tax: Not quite: taxes are an advantage. The disadvantage is that much profit goes back to the home country.
wrong.train: Not quite: training is an advantage. The disadvantage is that much profit goes back to the home country.

idk.hint: Two options help Nigeria. Which one takes money away?

steps.answerWhy: Much of the profit goes back to the TNC's home country, so less money helps Nigerians.

steps.question: An exam answer says "Shell brings jobs and money." How can it be improved?

options.text: Explain how: for example, taxes from Shell pay for schools and clinics
Add that Shell is a big company

steps.right: Yes: examiners want the process explained, not just stated.

wrong.other: Not quite: explain how, for example taxes pay for schools and clinics.
wrong.twice: Not quite: repeating adds nothing. Explain how: taxes from Shell pay for schools and clinics.
wrong.big: Not quite: that adds no understanding. Explain how: taxes pay for schools and clinics.

idk.hint: Examiners want to know how the jobs and money help development. Which option explains a link?

steps.answerWhy: A good answer explains how: taxes from Shell pay for schools and clinics, which helps development.

steps.prompt: In one line: give one advantage and one disadvantage of TNCs for Nigeria.
points: an advantage (jobs, skills, taxes, roads, technology)
a disadvantage (profits leave the country, few jobs from oil, oil spills, gas flaring)
steps.idk: No problem. A good line would be: TNCs give jobs and pay taxes, but much of the profit leaves Nigeria and oil spills pollute the Niger Delta.

steps.text: Nigeria sells mostly oil and gas abroad, and buys machines, vehicles and food. It used to trade mostly with Europe and the USA; now China and India are big partners too.
China has also lent money and built roads and railways in Nigeria, though some worry this leaves Nigeria in debt.

Political links have changed too. Nigeria is a Commonwealth member, but was suspended under military rule and welcomed back when elected government returned. It is a leading member of the African Union and ECOWAS.
Nigeria also receives aid: help on easy terms, as gifts or very cheap loans. Aid given by one government directly to another is called bilateral aid, such as the UK's help for girls' schooling.
Aid given through international organisations, such as the World Bank or the United Nations, is called multilateral aid.
Charities that run aid projects, such as handing out mosquito nets against malaria, are called NGOs: non-governmental organisations.

steps.question: The UK government pays for girls' schooling in Nigeria. What type of aid is this?
steps.right: Yes: one government directly to another is bilateral.

wrong.other: Not quite: bilateral aid, from one government directly to another.
wrong.multi: Not quite: multilateral goes through an international organisation. This is one government to another: bilateral.
wrong.micro: Not quite: microfinance is a small loan to start a business. This is bilateral aid.

idk.hint: Bi means two. How many governments are involved here?

steps.answerWhy: One government helping another directly is bilateral aid.

steps.text: Aid can save lives and pay for schools, clinics and clean water. But it can be wasted or stolen through corruption, and may not reach the poorest people.

steps.prompt: In one line: give one good impact of aid in Nigeria and one problem with it.
points: a good impact (schools, clinics, clean water, mosquito nets, saving lives)
a problem (wasted or stolen through corruption, may not reach the poorest)
steps.idk: No problem. A good line would be: aid pays for schools and mosquito nets, but some is lost to corruption.

keyPoints.heading: Environmental impacts and quality of life

steps.text: Economic development has costs for the environment. Oil spills kill fish and crops in the Niger Delta; factories and traffic pollute the air of Lagos; forests are cut down for farms and buildings.
In the Ogoni area of the delta, local people protested against oil pollution. Ken Saro-Wiwa, a writer who led those peaceful protests, was executed by the military government of the time.
Development has also changed people's quality of life: how good their lives are, in health, income, schooling, housing and safety.
Life expectancy in Nigeria rose from 47 years in 2000 to 55 in 2024, and infant mortality fell from 95 to 70 babies in every 1,000.

steps.question: Which piece of evidence shows quality of life in Nigeria improving?

options.text: Life expectancy rose from 47 to 55 years
Oil spills polluted the Niger Delta

steps.right: Yes: people living longer is clear evidence of a better quality of life.

wrong.other: Not quite: life expectancy rose from 47 to 55 years.
wrong.spill: Not quite: that is an environmental cost. Life expectancy rising from 47 to 55 shows improvement.
wrong.fuel: Not quite: that is about trade. Life expectancy rising from 47 to 55 shows improvement.

idk.hint: Quality of life is about health and living standards. Which option is about how long people live?

steps.answerWhy: Life expectancy rising from 47 to 55 years shows quality of life improving.

steps.text: But the gains are uneven. The south, with the oil and Lagos, is richer. The north has more poverty and fewer children in school.
Boko Haram, an armed extremist group in the north-east, has attacked towns and forced many people from their homes.

steps.prompt: In one line: how has economic development affected Nigeria? Give one gain and one cost.
points: a gain (longer lives, fewer infant deaths, more jobs in services)
a cost (oil pollution, air pollution, deforestation, or uneven gains between north and south)
steps.idk: No problem. A good line would be: people live longer, but oil spills have polluted the Niger Delta.

steps.text: Now for a short quiz: six questions on the whole lesson. Take your time.

steps.question: Quiz, question 1 of 6: what kind of country is Nigeria?

wrong.w1: Not quite: Nigeria is not rich enough to be an HIC. It is an NEE.
wrong.w2: Not quite: its economy is growing as industry builds up, so it is an NEE.

steps.answerWhy: Nigeria is an NEE, a newly emerging economy.

steps.question: Quiz, question 2 of 6: where does most of Nigeria's oil come from?

wrong.w1: Not quite: the north is dry grassland. The oil is in the Niger Delta.
wrong.w2: Not quite: Lagos is the biggest city. The oil is in the Niger Delta.

steps.answerWhy: Most of Nigeria's oil comes from the Niger Delta.

steps.question: Quiz, question 3 of 6: a soap factory is in which sector?
steps.right: Yes: it makes things, so secondary.

wrong.w1: Not quite: primary takes raw materials. A factory makes things: secondary.
wrong.w2: Not quite: tertiary is services. A factory makes things: secondary.

steps.answerWhy: Making things in factories is the secondary sector.

steps.question: Quiz, question 4 of 6: what is profit repatriation?

options.text: A foreign company sending profits back to its home country

wrong.other: Not quite: a foreign company sending profits back to its home country.

steps.answerWhy: Profit repatriation is a foreign company sending its profits back home.

steps.question: Quiz, question 5 of 6: aid given through the World Bank is…?
steps.right: Yes: through an international organisation, so multilateral.

wrong.w1: Not quite: bilateral is one government to another. Through the World Bank is multilateral.
wrong.w2: Not quite: debt relief cancels debt. Aid through the World Bank is multilateral.

steps.answerWhy: Aid through an international organisation is multilateral.

steps.question: Quiz, question 6 of 6: which is an environmental cost of oil in Nigeria?

options.text: Spills that kill fish and crops

wrong.other: Not quite: spills that kill fish and crops.
wrong.w1: Not quite: jobs are a benefit. Spills are an environmental cost.
wrong.w2: Not quite: tax is a benefit. Spills are an environmental cost.

steps.answerWhy: Oil spills kill fish and crops in the Niger Delta.

steps.text: That's the end of the quiz: you got {right} out of {n}.

end.text: The lesson is finished. Tap a button to go on.
